newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX crude ends sharply off on technical selling.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX crude ends sharply off on technical selling.

text.p: NYMEX crude was whipsawed Wednesday into a sharply lower finish after strength on inventory data crumbled into a sell-off when technical support levels were broken, traders said.
December crude settled 73 cents lower at $23.76 a barrel after rising as high as $24.95, up 46 cents on the day of its expiry. Due to the expiry, most traders focused on January crude's action.
"There were a lot of technical points that were broken in January (crude) that triggered selling," said Rocky D'Esposito of RJ Futures in New York.
Traders cited broken support of $24.00 and $23.80 in January as having accelerated selling.
Refined products were hit hard by the sell-off in crude, with December gasoline ending off two cents at 65.39 cents a gallon, and December heating oil ending off 1.59 cents at 72.09 cents a gallon.

Crude prices surged in the first part of Wednesday's session after the American Petroleum Institute (API) said Tuesday that crude stocks dropped 3.5 million barrels for the week ended November 15, putting stocks at a lean 9.92 million barrels below a year ago.
The oil complex started to weaken when gasoline began to register losses on the API report, said traders.
Though the API reported a draw in gasoline stocks, traders noted an increase in an already high output rate for gasoline which may signal stock builds in the future.
Gasoline ouput increased to 7.78 million barrels a day last week from 7.43 million barrels a day for the week ended November 8.

Another key part of Wednesday's sell-off was disappointing buying interest in December heating oil after it broke resistance of 74.50 cents a gallon, said Bob MacMinn, president of MPAS Inc in Toronto.
"74.50 was a huge number, but there was not the buying which was expected after we broke it," said MacMinn.

MacMinn said Wednesday's oil price action has brought spot crude into lower trading range of between $22.50 and $24.50. MacMinn said heating oil could break crude out of this range if there is a cold spell which spurs heavy heating oil demand.
-- Harry Milling, New York Energy Desk, 212-859-1761
